1: #!/usr/bin/env python3
2: """Grok epic-lane session canary — mint / questions / score / protocol.
3: 
4: Purpose
5: -------
6: Auto-compact compresses **working context** (lossy for nuance). Disk logs and
7: session-stream dual-writes survive; the model brain does not. This CLI freezes
8: durable anchors at cold-start and scores recall later so we **end the session
9: on measured rot**, not on compact count or a guessed token budget.
10: 
11: Policy (operational, not production-rollover)
12: ---------------------------------------------
13: - Mint **10** anchors from stream + handoff dual-write only (no git/PR scrape).
14: - Score with legacy ``context_canary``: ``--pass-ratio`` default **0.8** (8/10).
15: - FAIL-HANDOFF (rc 2) ⇒ write STATE AT HANDBACK, close stream lease, ``/quit``.
16: - First auto-compact is a **re-score trigger**, not an end signal by itself.
17: - ``score`` **auto-hydrates on PASS** (Sol Option D) so the operator never
18:   has to remember hydrate/restart for diary load; use ``--no-hydrate`` only
19:   for tests/debugging.
20: - Production identity rollover remains ``context_canary mint --snapshot`` (strict 10/10).
21: 
22: Paths (gitignored local; under ``.claude/<epic>-epic/canary/``)
23: ---------------------------------------------------------------
24:   probe.json       frozen ground truth (do not show answers to the scorer turn)
25:   questions.json   id → question only (agent answers from memory)
26:   answers.json     agent-written answers for score
27:   log.csv          (context_tokens, score) time series
28:   last_verdict.json  latest machine verdict
29: 
30: Usage
31: -----
32:   .venv/bin/python -m scripts.session_canary.grok_lane mint --epic atlas
33:   .venv/bin/python -m scripts.session_canary.grok_lane questions
34:   .venv/bin/python -m scripts.session_canary.grok_lane score \\
35:       --answers .claude/atlas-epic/canary/answers.json \\
36:       --context-tokens 250000 --model grok-4.6
37:   .venv/bin/python -m scripts.session_canary.grok_lane protocol --epic atlas
38:   .venv/bin/python -m scripts.session_canary.grok_lane status --epic atlas
39: """

81: # derive from issue_streams.yaml so epic succession needs no canary edit.
82: EPIC_STREAM_DEFAULTS: dict[str, str] = _epic_stream_defaults()

97: def _handoff_candidates(repo: Path, epic: str, preferred: list[str] | None = None) -> list[Path]:
98:     base = repo / ".claude" / f"{epic}-epic"
99:     names = [
100:         *(preferred or []),
101:         "INTERIM-DRIVER-HANDOFF.md",
102:         "CLAUDE-DRIVER-HANDOFF.md",
103:         "CODEX-DRIVER-HANDOFF.md",
104:     ]

108: def _read_text(path: Path, limit: int = 120_000) -> str:
109:     if not path.is_file():
110:         return ""
111:     return path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")[:limit]

114: def _clip(text: str, max_len: int = 220) -> str:
115:     text = " ".join(text.split())
116:     if len(text) <= max_len:
117:         return text
118:     return text[: max_len - 1].rstrip() + "…"

121: def _load_stream_entries(stream_id: str, *, limit: int = 40) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
122:     """Return [{type, body}, ...] from session stream; empty if store unavailable."""
123:     try:
124:         from agents_extensions.shared.session_streams.db import SessionStreamDatabase
125:         from agents_extensions.shared.session_streams.store import SessionStreamStore
126: 
127:         store = SessionStreamStore(SessionStreamDatabase())
128:         digest = store.load_digest(stream_id, limit=limit)
129:         out: list[dict[str, str]] = []
130:         for entry in list(digest.pinned) + list(digest.recent):
131:             body = (entry.body or "").strip()
132:             if not body:
133:                 continue
134:             out.append(
135:                 {
136:                     "type": getattr(entry.type, "value", str(entry.type)),
137:                     "body": body,
138:                 }
139:             )
140:         return out
141:     except Exception as exc:
142:         # Fail-open to handoff-only mint when stream DB is missing/unreadable.
143:         print(f"warning: session stream unavailable ({type(exc).__name__}: {exc})", file=sys.stderr)
144:         return []
145:

147: def _extract_handoff_bullets(md: str, *, heading_substrings: tuple[str, ...], limit: int = 12) -> list[str]:
148:     """Pull bullet lines under headings whose title contains any substring (case-insensitive)."""
149:     if not md:
150:         return []
151:     lines = md.splitlines()
152:     bullets: list[str] = []
153:     active = False
154:     for line in lines:
155:         if re.match(r"^#{1,4}\s+", line):
156:             title = re.sub(r"^#{1,4}\s+", "", line).strip().lower()
157:             active = any(s in title for s in heading_substrings)
158:             continue
159:         if not active:
160:             continue
161:         m = re.match(r"^\s*[-*]\s+(.+)$", line) or re.match(r"^\s*\d+\.\s+(.+)$", line)
162:         if m:
163:             item = m.group(1).strip()
164:             # strip markdown bold/links lightly
165:             item = re.sub(r"\*\*([^*]+)\*\*", r"\1", item)
166:             item = re.sub(r"\[([^\]]+)\]\([^)]+\)", r"\1", item)
167:             if item:
168:                 bullets.append(item)
169:             if len(bullets) >= limit:
170:                 break
171:     return bullets
172: 
173: 
174: def _build_facts(
175:     *,
176:     epic: str,
177:     stream_id: str,
178:     stream_entries: list[dict[str, str]],
179:     handoff_text: str,
180:     handoff_rel: str,
181: ) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
182:     """Build exactly 10 unique {id,q,a} facts from durable sources only."""
183:     facts: list[dict[str, str]] = []
184:     used_answers: set[str] = set()
185: 
186:     # Pre-extract working set so we can reserve probe slots (CF F001 on #5716).
187:     working_set = _extract_handoff_bullets(
188:         handoff_text,
189:         heading_substrings=("active working set", "working set"),
190:     )
191:     workset_reserve = min(2, len(working_set))
192: 
193:     def add(fid: str, q: str, a: str, *, reserve: int = 0) -> bool:
194:         """Add a fact if unique. Respect optional slot reservation for later workset."""
195:         if len(facts) >= N_ANCHORS - max(0, reserve):
196:             return False
197:         a_norm = _clip(a, 280)
198:         if not a_norm or a_norm in used_answers:
199:             return False
200:         if any(f["id"] == fid for f in facts):
201:             return False
202:         used_answers.add(a_norm)
203:         facts.append({"id": fid, "q": q, "a": a_norm})
204:         return True
205: 
206:     # 1) Session identity (always; never reserved against)
207:     add(
208:         "lane-stream",
209:         "What session stream id is this Grok lane driving?",
210:         stream_id,
211:     )
212:     add(
213:         "lane-epic",
214:         "What epic slug is this Grok lane bound to?",
215:         epic,
216:     )
217: 
218:     # 2) Pinned binding orders from stream (leave room for workset when present)
219:     pinned_orders = [e for e in stream_entries if e["type"] == "binding_order"]
220:     for i, entry in enumerate(pinned_orders[:4], start=1):
221:         if not add(
222:             f"bind-{i}",
223:             f"What is binding order #{i} for this lane (plain paraphrase of the frozen stream pin)?",
224:             entry["body"],
225:             reserve=workset_reserve,
226:         ):
227:             break
228: 
229:     # 3) Negative constraints from stream
230:     negs = [e for e in stream_entries if e["type"] == "negative_constraint"]
231:     for i, entry in enumerate(negs[:2], start=1):
232:         if not add(
233:             f"neg-{i}",
234:             f"What is negative constraint #{i} pinned on this stream?",
235:             entry["body"],
236:             reserve=workset_reserve,
237:         ):
238:             break
239: 
240:     # 4) Handoff dual-write: Next Drive (reserve workset slots after these)
241:     next_bullets = _extract_handoff_bullets(
242:         handoff_text,
243:         heading_substrings=("next drive", "next after", "next action", "in flight", "live session"),
244:     )
245:     for i, bullet in enumerate(next_bullets[:3], start=1):
246:         if not add(
247:             f"next-handoff-{i}",
248:             f"According to the dual-write handoff ({handoff_rel}), what is next-item #{i}?",
249:             bullet,
250:             reserve=workset_reserve,
251:         ):
252:             break
253: 
254:     # 4b) Active Working Set — reserved slots (load-bearing mid-flight facts)
255:     for i, bullet in enumerate(working_set[:2], start=1):
256:         add(
257:             f"workset-{i}",
258:             f"According to the dual-write handoff, what is active working-set fact #{i}?",
259:             bullet,
260:             reserve=0,
261:         )
262: 
263:     hands_off = _extract_handoff_bullets(
264:         handoff_text,
265:         heading_substrings=("hands-off", "handsoff", "do not", "out of scope"),
266:     )
267:     for i, bullet in enumerate(hands_off[:2], start=1):
268:         if not add(
269:             f"handsoff-{i}",
270:             f"According to the dual-write handoff, what is hands-off rule #{i}?",
271:             bullet,
272:             reserve=0,
273:         ):
274:             break
275: 
276:     # 5) Stream next_action fill remaining slots
277:     nexts = [e for e in stream_entries if e["type"] == "next_action"]
278:     for i, entry in enumerate(nexts[:3], start=1):
279:         if not add(
280:             f"next-stream-{i}",
281:             f"What next-action entry #{i} was recorded on the stream?",
282:             entry["body"],
283:         ):
284:             break
285: 
286:     # 6) Recent durable decisions from stream if still short
287:     decisions = [e for e in stream_entries if e["type"] == "decision"]
288:     for i, entry in enumerate(decisions[:3], start=1):
289:         if not add(
290:             f"decision-{i}",
291:             f"What decision #{i} was recorded on the stream?",
292:             entry["body"],
293:         ):
294:             break
295: 
296:     # 7) Recent state if still short (still dual-written stream entries — durable)
297:     states = [e for e in stream_entries if e["type"] == "state"]
298:     for i, entry in enumerate(reversed(states[-6:]), start=1):
299:         if not add(
300:             f"state-{i}",
301:             f"What recent state note #{i} is on the stream (paraphrase the frozen text)?",
302:             entry["body"],
303:         ):
304:             break
305: 
306:     if len(facts) < N_ANCHORS:
307:         raise SystemExit(
308:             f"error: could only derive {len(facts)}/{N_ANCHORS} durable anchors; "
309:             "open a stream session and dual-write handoff next/hands-off sections, then re-mint"
310:         )
311: 
312:     # Exactly 10 — prefer earliest (highest-trust: identity + pins)
313:     return facts[:N_ANCHORS]

626: def emit_hydrate_capsule(
627:     *,
628:     repo: Path,
629:     epic: str,
630:     stream_id: str | None = None,
631:     handoff: str | Path | None = None,
632:     out_dir: Path | None = None,
633:     max_tokens: int = 1400,
634:     max_stamps: int = 3,
635:     stream_limit: int = 5,
636:     no_stream: bool = False,
637:     write: bool = False,
638:     print_stdout: bool = True,
639:     banner: str | None = None,
640:     preferred: list[str] | None = None,
641: ) -> tuple[int, dict]:
642:     """Build and optionally print/write a Sol Option-D hydrate capsule.
643: 
644:     Returns ``(rc, meta)``. ``rc`` is 0 on success, 1 on missing diary, 2 on
645:     visible identity/next-drive gap. Fail-open callers may ignore rc.
646:     """
647:     from scripts.session_canary import diary as diary_mod
648: 
649:     epic = epic.strip().lower()
650:     stream_id = (stream_id or EPIC_STREAM_DEFAULTS.get(epic, "epic:N")).strip()
651:     handoff_path = diary_mod.resolve_handoff_path(repo, epic, handoff, preferred=preferred)
652:     if not handoff_path.is_file():
653:         print(f"error: diary handoff missing: {handoff_path}", file=sys.stderr)
654:         return 1, {"error": "missing_handoff", "handoff": str(handoff_path)}
655:     diary_text = handoff_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
656:     stream_tail = ""
657:     if not no_stream:
658:         stream_tail = diary_mod.try_stream_tail_text(stream_id, limit=int(stream_limit))
659:     capsule, meta = diary_mod.build_hydrate_capsule(
660:         diary_text,
661:         epic=epic,
662:         stream_id=stream_id,
663:         stream_tail=stream_tail,
664:         max_tokens=int(max_tokens),
665:         max_stamps=int(max_stamps),
666:     )
667:     meta = dict(meta)
668:     meta["handoff"] = str(handoff_path)
669:     if print_stdout:
670:         if banner:
671:             print(banner)
672:             print()
673:         sys.stdout.write(capsule)
674:         if not capsule.endswith("\n"):
675:             sys.stdout.write("\n")
676:     print(
677:         f"hydrate_meta: tokens≈{meta.get('approx_tokens')} chars={meta.get('chars')} "
678:         f"sha={meta.get('capsule_sha256')} dropped={meta.get('dropped_sections')} "
679:         f"gap={meta.get('visible_gap')}",
680:         file=sys.stderr,
681:     )
682:     if write:
683:         dest = out_dir if out_dir is not None else _canary_dir(repo, epic)
684:         dest.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
685:         out_path = dest / "hydrate.md"
686:         tmp = out_path.with_suffix(".md.tmp")
687:         tmp.write_text(capsule, encoding="utf-8")
688:         meta_path = dest / "hydrate_meta.json"
689:         meta_path.write_text(
690:             json.dumps({"written_at": _utc_now(), **meta}, indent=2) + "\n",
691:             encoding="utf-8",
692:         )
693:         tmp.replace(out_path)
694:         print(f"hydrate receipt -> {out_path}", file=sys.stderr)
695:         meta["receipt"] = str(out_path)
696:     rc = 2 if meta.get("visible_gap") else 0
697:     return rc, meta

1: #!/usr/bin/env python3
2: """Block staged plan edits that skip versioning or add backup snapshots."""
3: 
4: from __future__ import annotations
5: 
6: import argparse
7: import re
8: import subprocess
9: import sys
10: from pathlib import Path
11: 
12: import yaml
13: 
14: PLAN_PATH_RE = re.compile(r"^curriculum/[^/]+/plans/.+\.yaml$")
15: AUTO_FIX_TAG = "[auto-fix-plan-vocab]"
16: METADATA_ONLY_FIELDS = {
17:     "module",
18:     "sequence",
19:     "slug",
20:     "slug_intentional",
21:     "level",
22:     "connects_to",
23:     "prerequisites",
24: }
25: YAML_BACKUP_SUFFIXES = (".yaml.bak", ".yml.bak", ".yaml.orig", ".yml.orig")
26: 
27: 
28: def _run_git(repo_root: Path, *args: str, check: bool = True) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:
29:     """Run a git command from the target repository."""
30:     result = subprocess.run(
31:         ["git", *args],
32:         cwd=repo_root,
33:         check=False,
34:         capture_output=True,
35:         text=True,
36:     )
37:     if check and result.returncode != 0:
38:         raise RuntimeError(result.stderr.strip() or f"git {' '.join(args)} failed")
39:     return result
40: 
41: 
42: def _repo_root() -> Path:
43:     """Resolve the repository root from the current working directory."""
44:     result = _run_git(Path.cwd(), "rev-parse", "--show-toplevel")
45:     return Path(result.stdout.strip())
46: 
47: 
48: def _staged_files(repo_root: Path) -> list[str]:
49:     """Return staged file paths relative to the repository root."""
50:     result = _run_git(repo_root, "diff", "--cached", "--name-only", "--diff-filter=AM")
51:     return [line for line in result.stdout.splitlines() if line]
52: 
53: 
54: def _is_plan_path(path: str) -> bool:
55:     """True when the staged path is a curriculum plan YAML file."""
56:     return bool(PLAN_PATH_RE.match(path))
57: 
58: 
59: def _is_yaml_backup_path(path: str) -> bool:
60:     """True when a staged path is a YAML backup artifact."""
61:     return path.endswith(YAML_BACKUP_SUFFIXES)
62: 
63: 
64: def _git_blob_exists(repo_root: Path, spec: str) -> bool:
65:     """Return whether a git object spec resolves successfully."""
66:     result = subprocess.run(
67:         ["git", "cat-file", "-e", spec],
68:         cwd=repo_root,
69:         check=False,
70:         capture_output=True,
71:         text=True,
72:     )
73:     return result.returncode == 0
74: 
75: 
76: def _read_git_blob(repo_root: Path, spec: str) -> str:
77:     """Read text content from a git object spec."""
78:     result = _run_git(repo_root, "show", spec)
79:     return result.stdout
80: 
81: 
82: def _read_commit_message(repo_root: Path, commit_msg_file: str | None) -> str:
83:     """Read the in-flight commit message when it is available."""
84:     if commit_msg_file:
85:         path = Path(commit_msg_file)
86:     else:
87:         result = _run_git(repo_root, "rev-parse", "--git-path", "COMMIT_EDITMSG")
88:         path = repo_root / result.stdout.strip()
89: 
90:     if not path.exists():
91:         return ""
92:     return path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
93: 
94: 
95: def _parse_version(content: str, label: str) -> str:
96:     """Extract the plan version from YAML content."""
97:     try:
98:         data = yaml.safe_load(content)
99:     except yaml.YAMLError as exc:
100:         raise ValueError(f"{label}: failed to parse YAML: {exc}") from exc
101: 
102:     if not isinstance(data, dict):
103:         raise ValueError(f"{label}: expected a YAML mapping at the document root")
104: 
105:     version = data.get("version")
106:     if version is None or str(version).strip() == "":
107:         raise ValueError(f"{label}: missing version field")
108: 
109:     return str(version).strip()
110: 
111: 
112: def _parse_plan(content: str, label: str) -> dict:
113:     """Parse a plan YAML document as a mapping."""
114:     try:
115:         data = yaml.safe_load(content)
116:     except yaml.YAMLError as exc:
117:         raise ValueError(f"{label}: failed to parse YAML: {exc}") from exc
118: 
119:     if not isinstance(data, dict):
120:         raise ValueError(f"{label}: expected a YAML mapping at the document root")
121: 
122:     return data
123: 
124: 
125: def _version_parts(version: str) -> tuple[int, ...] | None:
126:     """Parse a dotted numeric version, returning None for custom schemes."""
127:     parts = version.split(".")
128:     if not parts or any(not part.isdigit() for part in parts):
129:         return None
130:     return tuple(int(part) for part in parts)
131: 
132: 
133: def _is_version_increment(old_version: str, new_version: str) -> bool:
134:     """Return true when the new version is strictly newer than the old one."""
135:     old_parts = _version_parts(old_version)
136:     new_parts = _version_parts(new_version)
137:     if old_parts is None or new_parts is None:
138:         return new_version != old_version
139: 
140:     width = max(len(old_parts), len(new_parts))
141:     return old_parts + (0,) * (width - len(old_parts)) < new_parts + (0,) * (width - len(new_parts))
142: 
143: 
144: def _is_metadata_only_edit(old_content: str, new_content: str) -> bool:
145:     """Return true when only ordering/reference metadata changed.
146: 
147:     Curriculum order repairs need to update plan ids and dependency links
148:     without inventing backup files. Content-bearing plan edits still need the
149:     normal version bump and previous-content snapshot.
150:     """
151:     old_plan = _parse_plan(old_content, "old plan")
152:     new_plan = _parse_plan(new_content, "new plan")
153: 
154:     for key in METADATA_ONLY_FIELDS:
155:         old_plan.pop(key, None)
156:         new_plan.pop(key, None)
157: 
158:     return old_plan == new_plan
159: 
160: 
161: def _collect_errors(repo_root: Path) -> list[str]:
162:     """Validate staged plan edits against the immutability rule."""
163:     staged = _staged_files(repo_root)
164:     errors: list[str] = []
165: 
166:     for path in staged:
167:         if _is_yaml_backup_path(path):
168:             errors.append(
169:                 f"{path}: YAML backup artifacts are no longer tracked; bump the plan version instead"
170:             )
171: 
172:     for plan_path in staged:
173:         if not _is_plan_path(plan_path):
174:             continue
175: 
176:         head_spec = f"HEAD:{plan_path}"
177:         if not _git_blob_exists(repo_root, head_spec):
178:             # New plans have no previous version to compare against.
179:             continue
180: 
181:         old_content = _read_git_blob(repo_root, head_spec)
182:         new_content = _read_git_blob(repo_root, f":{plan_path}")
183:         try:
184:             if _is_metadata_only_edit(old_content, new_content):
185:                 continue
186:         except ValueError as exc:
187:             errors.append(str(exc))
188:             continue
189: 
190:         try:
191:             old_version = _parse_version(old_content, plan_path)
192:             new_version = _parse_version(new_content, plan_path)
193:         except ValueError as exc:
194:             errors.append(str(exc))
195:             continue
196: 
197:         if not _is_version_increment(old_version, new_version):
198:             errors.append(f"{plan_path}: version not incremented ({old_version} -> {new_version})")
199: 
200:     return errors
201: 
202: 
203: def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
204:     """CLI entrypoint."""
205:     parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
206:         description="Enforce version bumps and block backup artifacts for staged curriculum plan edits."
207:     )
208:     parser.add_argument(
209:         "commit_msg_file",
210:         nargs="?",
211:         help="Path to COMMIT_EDITMSG from the commit-msg hook stage.",
212:     )
213:     args = parser.parse_args(argv)
214: 
215:     repo_root = _repo_root()
216:     if AUTO_FIX_TAG in _read_commit_message(repo_root, args.commit_msg_file):
217:         return 0
218: 
219:     errors = _collect_errors(repo_root)
220:     if not errors:
221:         return 0
222: 
223:     print(
224:         "Plans are versioned - content changes need an incremented `version:` field.",
225:         file=sys.stderr,
226:     )
227:     print(
228:         "Do not stage `.yaml.bak` plan backups; previous versions live in git history "
229:         "(`git show HEAD:<path>`).",
230:         file=sys.stderr,
231:     )
232:     print(
233:         f"Exception: metadata-only fields {sorted(METADATA_ONLY_FIELDS)} may change without a version bump.",
234:         file=sys.stderr,
235:     )
236:     print(
237:         f"Exception: pipeline auto-fix commits use `{AUTO_FIX_TAG}` tag.",
238:         file=sys.stderr,
239:     )
240:     print(
241:         "See: agents_extensions/shared/rules/non-negotiable-rules.md §7",
242:         file=sys.stderr,
243:     )
244:     print("", file=sys.stderr)
245:     for error in errors:
246:         print(f"- {error}", file=sys.stderr)
247: 
248:     return 1
249: 
250:

252:     raise SystemExit(main())

1: #!/usr/bin/env python3
2: """Unexpected repo-root entry guard (#6863).
3: 
4: A transport/quoting defect once materialized garbage directories at the repo
5: root — names that were verbatim opencode/ACP event-stream JSON lines and
6: word-split tokens of them (a literal ``-rf`` among them). Empty directories
7: are invisible to ``git status``, so this class of pollution sat undetected;
8: one of them even grew a shadow fleet-comms DB and swallowed a message.
9: 
10: This guard deterministically lists the primary checkout's top-level entries
11: and reports any that are neither tracked nor gitignored. It is ALERT-ONLY:
12: nothing is ever deleted here — garbage root entries are forensic evidence and
13: removal is an explicit human decision.
14: 
15: Surfaces:
16: * Session-start sweep: ``agents_extensions/shared/hooks/session-setup.sh``
17:   invokes this module bounded and surfaces findings as an ISSUE line.
18: * Advisory CLI: ``python -m scripts.hygiene.root_entry_guard [--strict]``.
19: """
20: 
21: from __future__ import annotations
22: 
23: import argparse
24: import json
25: import subprocess
26: import sys
27: from pathlib import Path
28: 
29: # Dual-flavor import: delegate workers put only ``scripts/`` on sys.path (see
30: # the note in scripts/guardrails/worktree_containment.py).
31: try:
32:     from scripts.common.git_context import sanitized_git_env
33:     from scripts.guardrails.worktree_containment import resolve_main_root
34: except ImportError:  # scripts/ on sys.path (stripped flavor)
35:     from common.git_context import sanitized_git_env  # type: ignore[no-redef]
36:     from guardrails.worktree_containment import resolve_main_root  # type: ignore[no-redef]
37: 
38: __all__ = ["UnexpectedEntry", "main", "scan_unexpected_root_entries"]
39: 
40: 
41: class UnexpectedEntry:
42:     """One top-level repo-root entry that git does not expect."""
43: 
44:     def __init__(self, name: str, *, kind: str, empty_dir: bool) -> None:
45:         self.name = name
46:         self.kind = kind
47:         # Empty dirs are invisible to git status; everything else git can see.
48:         self.git_invisible = empty_dir
49: 
50:     def to_dict(self) -> dict:
51:         return {
52:             "name": self.name,
53:             "kind": self.kind,
54:             "git_invisible": self.git_invisible,
55:         }
56: 
57: 
58: def _run_git(root: Path, *args: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:
59:     return subprocess.run(
60:         ["git", "-C", str(root), *args],
61:         capture_output=True,
62:         text=True,
63:         check=False,
64:         env=sanitized_git_env(),
65:     )
66: 
67: 
68: def _tracked_top_level_names(root: Path) -> set[str]:
69:     """First path component of every tracked file (NUL-safe)."""
70:     proc = _run_git(root, "ls-files", "-z")
71:     if proc.returncode != 0:
72:         raise RuntimeError(
73:             f"git ls-files failed under {root}: "
74:             f"{(proc.stderr or proc.stdout or 'unknown error').strip()}"
75:         )
76:     names: set[str] = set()
77:     for path in proc.stdout.split("\0"):
78:         if path:
79:             names.add(path.split("/", 1)[0])
80:     return names
81: 
82: 
83: def _is_ignored(root: Path, name: str) -> bool:
84:     # -q: exit 0 == ignored, 1 == not ignored, 128 == error.
85:     proc = _run_git(root, "check-ignore", "-q", "--", name)
86:     return proc.returncode == 0
87: 
88: 
89: def _classify(entry: Path) -> tuple[str, bool]:
90:     """(kind, empty_dir) for a top-level entry; symlinks are not followed."""
91:     if entry.is_symlink():
92:         return "symlink", False
93:     if entry.is_dir():
94:         try:
95:             empty = not any(entry.iterdir())
96:         except OSError:
97:             empty = False
98:         return "dir", empty
99:     return "file", False
100: 
101: 
102: def scan_unexpected_root_entries(repo_root: Path | None = None) -> list[UnexpectedEntry]:
103:     """Top-level entries of the primary checkout that git neither tracks nor ignores.
104: 
105:     ``repo_root`` may point anywhere inside the repo (a worktree cwd included);
106:     the scan always targets the primary checkout that owns the shared ``.git``.
107:     Raises if the anchor is not inside a git repository.
108:     """
109:     root = resolve_main_root(repo_root if repo_root is not None else Path.cwd())
110:     tracked = _tracked_top_level_names(root)
111: 
112:     unexpected: list[UnexpectedEntry] = []
113:     for entry in sorted(root.iterdir(), key=lambda p: p.name):
114:         name = entry.name
115:         if name == ".git" or name in tracked:
116:             continue
117:         if _is_ignored(root, name):
118:             continue
119:         kind, empty_dir = _classify(entry)
120:         unexpected.append(UnexpectedEntry(name, kind=kind, empty_dir=empty_dir))
121:     return unexpected
122: 
123: 
124: def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
125:     parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
126:         description=(
127:             "Alert on unexpected top-level entries in the primary checkout "
128:             "(including empty dirs git cannot see). Advisory by default; "
129:             "never deletes anything (#6863)."
130:         )
131:     )
132:     parser.add_argument(
133:         "--repo-root",
134:         type=Path,
135:         default=None,
136:         help="Anchor path inside the repo (default: cwd); scan targets the primary checkout.",
137:     )
138:     parser.add_argument("--json", action="store_true", help="Emit a JSON report.")
139:     parser.add_argument(
140:         "--strict",
141:         action="store_true",
142:         help="Exit 1 when unexpected entries exist (default: always exit 0).",
143:     )
144:     args = parser.parse_args(argv)
145: 
146:     root = resolve_main_root(args.repo_root if args.repo_root is not None else Path.cwd())
147:     unexpected = scan_unexpected_root_entries(root)
148:     report = {
149:         "repo_root": str(root),
150:         "unexpected_count": len(unexpected),
151:         "unexpected": [entry.to_dict() for entry in unexpected],
152:     }
153:     if args.json:
154:         print(json.dumps(report, indent=2))
155:     elif unexpected:
156:         print("UNEXPECTED repo-root entries (inspect manually; never auto-deleted, #6863):")
157:         for entry in unexpected:
158:             invis = " [git-invisible empty dir]" if entry.git_invisible else ""
159:             print(f"  - {entry.name} ({entry.kind}){invis}")
160:     else:
161:         print("Root hygiene OK: no unexpected top-level entries.")
162:     return 1 if (args.strict and unexpected) else 0
163: 
164: 
165: if __name__ == "__main__":
166:     sys.exit(main())

1: #!/usr/bin/env python3
2: """Lane disk-retention scanner (#4956).
3: 
4: Policy (operator 2026-07-11):
5: - Each lane cleans **its own** session stores and dispatch worktrees.
6: - Dispatch worktrees that are merged → reap.
7: - Dirty/unpushed worktrees older than **72h** → push+PR or declare abandonable.
8: - Sessions/logs older than **14d** → archive then delete (manual / Drive).
9: 
10: This script is **read-only by default** (``--dry-run``). It never deletes
11: another lane's uncommitted work. Use ``--json`` for machine-readable output.
12: """
13: 
14: from __future__ import annotations
15: 
16: import argparse
17: import json
18: import subprocess
19: import sys
20: import time
21: from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass
22: from pathlib import Path
23: 
24: REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
25: DEFAULT_WORKTREE_STALE_HOURS = 72
26: DEFAULT_SESSION_STALE_DAYS = 14
27: 
28: 
29: @dataclass(frozen=True)
30: class WorktreeReport:
31:     path: str
32:     branch: str
33:     age_hours: float
34:     dirty: bool
35:     ahead_of_remote: bool
36:     recommendation: str
37: 
38: 
39: def _git(args: list[str], *, cwd: Path) -> str:
40:     result = subprocess.run(
41:         ["git", *args],
42:         cwd=str(cwd),
43:         capture_output=True,
44:         text=True,
45:         check=False,
46:     )
47:     return (result.stdout or "").strip()
48: 
49: 
50: def scan_dispatch_worktrees(
51:     *,
52:     repo_root: Path = REPO_ROOT,
53:     stale_hours: float = DEFAULT_WORKTREE_STALE_HOURS,
54:     now: float | None = None,
55: ) -> list[WorktreeReport]:
56:     """Scan ``.worktrees/dispatch/**`` for stale / dirty / merged candidates."""
57:     root = repo_root / ".worktrees" / "dispatch"
58:     if not root.is_dir():
59:         return []
60:     clock = now if now is not None else time.time()
61:     reports: list[WorktreeReport] = []
62:     for agent_dir in sorted(p for p in root.iterdir() if p.is_dir()):
63:         for task_dir in sorted(p for p in agent_dir.iterdir() if p.is_dir()):
64:             git_dir = task_dir / ".git"
65:             if not git_dir.exists():
66:                 continue
67:             mtime = task_dir.stat().st_mtime
68:             age_hours = max((clock - mtime) / 3600.0, 0.0)
69:             branch = _git(["rev-parse", "--abbrev-ref", "HEAD"], cwd=task_dir) or "(unknown)"
70:             status = _git(["status", "--porcelain"], cwd=task_dir)
71:             dirty = bool(status)
72:             ahead = False
73:             counts = _git(["rev-list", "--left-right", "--count", "@{u}...HEAD"], cwd=task_dir)
74:             if counts and "\t" in counts:
75:                 _behind, ahead_s = counts.split("\t", 1)
76:                 try:
77:                     ahead = int(ahead_s) > 0
78:                 except ValueError:
79:                     ahead = False
80:             if age_hours < stale_hours and not dirty:
81:                 rec = "ok"
82:             elif dirty and age_hours >= stale_hours:
83:                 rec = "stale-dirty: push+PR or mark abandonable on tracking issue, then reap"
84:             elif ahead and age_hours >= stale_hours:
85:                 rec = "stale-unpushed: push branch / open PR or abandon + worktree remove"
86:             elif age_hours >= stale_hours:
87:                 rec = "stale-clean: candidate for worktree remove if PR merged"
88:             else:
89:                 rec = "active-dirty: finish or checkpoint soon"
90:             reports.append(
91:                 WorktreeReport(
92:                     path=str(task_dir.relative_to(repo_root)),
93:                     branch=branch,
94:                     age_hours=round(age_hours, 1),
95:                     dirty=dirty,
96:                     ahead_of_remote=ahead,
97:                     recommendation=rec,
98:                 )
99:             )
100:     return reports
101: 
102: 
103: def scan_home_session_hints(
104:     *,
105:     stale_days: float = DEFAULT_SESSION_STALE_DAYS,
106: ) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
107:     """Non-destructive size/age hints for known session roots (home only)."""
108:     home = Path.home()
109:     candidates = [
110:         home / ".codex",
111:         home / ".claude",
112:         home / ".cursor",
113:         home / ".grok",
114:     ]
115:     clock = time.time()
116:     out: list[dict[str, object]] = []
117:     for path in candidates:
118:         if not path.exists():
119:             continue
120:         try:
121:             size = sum(f.stat().st_size for f in path.rglob("*") if f.is_file())
122:         except OSError:
123:             size = -1
124:         mtime = path.stat().st_mtime
125:         age_days = max((clock - mtime) / 86400.0, 0.0)
126:         out.append(
127:             {
128:                 "path": str(path),
129:                 "size_gb": round(size / (1024**3), 2) if size >= 0 else None,
130:                 "age_days": round(age_days, 1),
131:                 "recommendation": (
132:                     f"archive sessions older than {stale_days:g}d to Drive, then delete locally"
133:                     if age_days >= stale_days
134:                     else "within retention window"
135:                 ),
136:             }
137:         )
138:     return out
139: 
140: 
141: def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
142:     parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
143:     parser.add_argument("--repo-root", type=Path, default=REPO_ROOT)
144:     parser.add_argument("--stale-hours", type=float, default=DEFAULT_WORKTREE_STALE_HOURS)
145:     parser.add_argument("--session-stale-days", type=float, default=DEFAULT_SESSION_STALE_DAYS)
146:     parser.add_argument("--json", action="store_true", help="Machine-readable JSON report")
147:     parser.add_argument(
148:         "--include-home",
149:         action="store_true",
150:         help="Also scan ~/.codex ~/.claude ~/.cursor ~/.grok size hints (read-only)",
151:     )
152:     args = parser.parse_args(argv)
153: 
154:     worktrees = scan_dispatch_worktrees(
155:         repo_root=args.repo_root,
156:         stale_hours=args.stale_hours,
157:     )
158:     home = scan_home_session_hints(stale_days=args.session_stale_days) if args.include_home else []
159: 
160:     if args.json:
161:         print(
162:             json.dumps(
163:                 {
164:                     "worktrees": [asdict(w) for w in worktrees],
165:                     "home_sessions": home,
166:                     "policy": {
167:                         "worktree_stale_hours": args.stale_hours,
168:                         "session_stale_days": args.session_stale_days,
169:                         "mutate": False,
170:                     },
171:                 },
172:                 indent=2,
173:                 sort_keys=True,
174:             )
175:         )
176:         return 0
177: 
178:     print(f"Dispatch worktrees under {args.repo_root / '.worktrees' / 'dispatch'} "
179:           f"(stale ≥ {args.stale_hours:g}h): {len(worktrees)}")
180:     for w in worktrees:
181:         flags = []
182:         if w.dirty:
183:             flags.append("dirty")
184:         if w.ahead_of_remote:
185:             flags.append("ahead")
186:         flag_s = f" [{','.join(flags)}]" if flags else ""
187:         print(f"  {w.path}  branch={w.branch}  age={w.age_hours}h{flag_s}")
188:         print(f"    → {w.recommendation}")
189:     if home:
190:         print("\nHome session roots (hints only):")
191:         for row in home:
192:             print(f"  {row['path']}  ~{row['size_gb']} GiB  age={row['age_days']}d")
193:             print(f"    → {row['recommendation']}")
194:     print(
195:         "\nNo files were deleted. Reap merged worktrees with "
196:         "`git worktree remove …` after PR merge; archive sessions to Drive per #4956."
197:     )
198:     return 0
199: 
200: 
201: if __name__ == "__main__":
202:     sys.exit(main())

2: 
3: Background: a timeout-less ``subprocess.*`` hang held a CI runner for 357 minutes
4: (run ``30109965086``) because three guards were missing at once: call-site
5: ``timeout=``, job ``timeout-minutes``, and ``pytest-timeout``. Job caps landed in
6: PR #5735; ``pytest-timeout`` is pinned in ``requirements*.txt`` and enforced via
7: ``pyproject.toml`` (``timeout = 120``, ``timeout_method = "thread"``) plus the
8: CI pytest invocation. This module keeps the *call-site* fence from regrowing and
9: proves a hang fails fast *and names the test*.
10: 
11: ``subprocess.Popen`` cannot take ``timeout=`` at construction; callers must bound
12: ``.wait()`` / ``.communicate()`` (or an equivalent deadline). The AST guard below
13: covers ``run`` / ``check_output`` / ``call`` / ``check_call`` only.
14: """

17: 
18: import ast
19: import os
20: import re
21: import subprocess
22: import textwrap
23: from collections import Counter, defaultdict

31:

33: 
34: _REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
35: _TESTS_ROOT = _REPO_ROOT / "tests"
36: _SCRIPTS_ROOT = _REPO_ROOT / "scripts"
37: _ALLOWLIST_PATH = _SCRIPTS_ROOT / "ci" / "subprocess_timeout_allowlist.txt"
